task:
Build a complete playable browser GUI chess application for two human players sharing one computer, with no CPU opponent. Use Python, the standard-library HTTP server, embedded HTML/CSS/JavaScript, and the established python-chess dependency (already installed in this benchmark environment). Disclose python-chess in requirements.txt and README.md. Do not reimplement or simplify chess rules. No CDN or network assets.

Required files: chess_logic.py, chess_gui.py, main.py, test_chess.py, README.md, RunningGUIDE.txt, requirements.txt. Keep files concise and complete, one explicitly named file per model response when possible, to fit the response limit.

Public engine contract: chess_logic.py exports Game(fen=None). None means the standard initial chess position. A supplied FEN must initialize that position and allow known-position testing. Game.move(uci) accepts a legal UCI move string (e2e4, e1g1, e7e8n etc), applies it, and returns state(). Illegal moves, wrong-turn moves, invalid syntax and moves after game over raise ValueError without changing the position. Game.reset() restores the initial board and returns state(). Game.state() returns a JSON-compatible dict with: fen (full FEN), turn ('white'/'black'), pieces (dict mapping algebraic squares to standard piece symbols P,N,B,R,Q,K and lowercase black pieces), legal_moves (list of legal UCI strings), status ('playing','check','checkmate','stalemate','draw'), winner (None/'white'/'black'). Do not expose direct king capture as legal. Support all standard moves, captures, king safety and pins, check, checkmate, stalemate, castling restrictions, en passant availability, and promotion to queen/rook/bishop/knight. Treat claimable repetition/fifty-move and insufficient-material positions as draws. Use python-chess for legal move validation and outcomes.

HTTP contract: chess_gui.py exports create_server(host, port), returning a standard-library HTTPServer or ThreadingHTTPServer, without starting it on import. Every new server owns a fresh Game. GET / serves the complete browser GUI. GET /state returns Game.state() JSON. POST /move with JSON {"uci":"e2e4"} applies a move and returns state; malformed/illegal input returns HTTP 400 JSON {"error":"helpful message"}, leaving the position intact. POST /reset resets the game and returns state. Also provide POST /position with JSON {"fen":"..."} to load a test position using the same engine and return state; this is used to exercise special-move and endgame GUI behavior. Bound request sizes and handle bad JSON helpfully.

GUI: visible 8x8 board, light/dark alternating colors, all standard pieces clearly represented with Unicode chess symbols plus accessible labels. Use square button IDs sq-a8 through sq-h1 and data-square="a8" etc; set each square's data-piece attribute to the current piece symbol or empty string. Board container id=board; game-status element id=status; new-game button id=new-game; error display id=error. Clicking your piece marks its square with class selected, and marks legal destination squares with class legal. Clicking a legal destination POSTs a move, rerenders pieces, updates turn/status, and clears selection. Promotion uses a visible select id=promotion with option values q,r,b,n and meaningful piece names; use the chosen value for promotion moves. Captures and check/checkmate/stalemate/draw must appear in the actual interface. State must be loaded from the server and all moves validated by the engine. New game resets everything. Board should fit a normal desktop browser and include labels/instructions for two-player play.

Launch contract: main.py supports --host (default 127.0.0.1) and --port (default 8765), starts create_server(...).serve_forever() only under a main guard. Document exactly: python main.py --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765, then open http://127.0.0.1:8765. Document dependency installation, controls, promotion choice, supported draws, tests and stopping the server. All modules must import without opening windows or starting servers.

test_chess.py must contain real unittest.TestCase tests that exercise the engine, illegal input, check/mate/stalemate, castling, en passant and all promotion choices. Run those tests. Fix your own application based on real tool feedback within the given budget. Independent acceptance tests will launch a real browser, click squares, compare states to known chess positions, and require actual behavior. Do not edit the caller's acceptance checker. Do not start an indefinite server in a shell block; acceptance launches and cleans it up.

checks.requirement: Independent chess behavior and documented launch acceptance
